qc.scope: BRIEF-6.md Part D only: eight forest floor bases. Other art is comparison/context, without verdicts.
performed: Each base tiled 3x3 at 1x and nearest-neighbour 4x; wrap intersection also examined at 4x.
Every individual file examined at nearest-neighbour 8x.
Every base composited beneath a deterministic, varied forest at 1x and 4x.
Compared with named forest/ground references, approved markers, round-2 tiles, paddies, and all seasonal grass/plains bases with their eight details.
Checked dimensions, opacity, pixel edges, noise, shape readability, lighting, ground darkness, palette fit, seasonal content, repeats and similarity.
qc.not_applicable: No Part D peaks, ridges, crater props, ruins, cyberpunk city tiles, one-cell tiles or new tree crowns. Peak lattice/range and 8x2 random one-cell tiling are therefore not applicable; identical-crown judgments are outside this review.
qc.tree_context: Broadleaf: out/treeline_forest-0..7 and @autumn versions. Conifer: reference/current-fantasy-treeline_conifer_forest.png. Summer broadleaf silhouettes also used for spring/winter ground-readability checks, because no matching spring/winter broadleaf set exists in out/. Unseasonal comparator foliage is not a floor defect.
qc.format: All eight files are 288x288, fully opaque, with 6-8 solid palette colours. Opaque coverage is appropriate for a repeating floor. No visible blur, antialiasing, alpha fringe, halo, placement defect or conflicting directional light found in the floor pixels.
qc.darkness: All seasonal floors are darker than matching approved grass. Mean Rec.709 RGB luma: forest 76.28/76.27/70.57/129.38 and conifer 62.14/69.17/65.54/126.99 (summer/spring/autumn/winter), versus grass 111.65/152.31/120.05/240.86.
qc.similarity: No exact duplicate files. Shared subdued moss/litter vocabulary in non-winter seasons is acceptable for shaded floor; it does not create identical crowns or a conspicuous stamped grid.

pass_evidence.forest-floor-base: Low-contrast olive moss and sparse litter remain subordinate beneath the approved broadleaf trees; repeat joins do not draw a grid at map scale.
pass_evidence.forest@spring-floor-base: Fresher moss stays dark enough for shade; clean hard pixels, calm tiling, and readable overlaid trees.
pass_evidence.forest@autumn-floor-base: Sparse ochre fallen-leaf marks on subdued olive ground complement the varied approved autumn trees; no flat orange wash.

forest_floor.winter: Fail: busy raised-looking snow islands and a conspicuous repeated pattern.

pass_evidence.conifer_forest-floor-base: Dark blue-green shade with restrained moss/needle marks supports the reference conifers without adding crowns or competing highlights.
pass_evidence.conifer_forest@spring-floor-base: Sparse fresh moss and tiny needle/litter marks preserve quiet shaded gaps and clear tree silhouettes.
pass_evidence.conifer_forest@autumn-floor-base: Muted brown needle streaks provide autumn litter without turning evergreen ground orange; remains calm in repeat and forest composites.

conifer_forest_floor.winter: Fail: high-contrast camouflage pattern competes with trees and advertises the repeat.

fail.name: conifer_forest@winter-floor-base
fail.problems: At 1x the floor reads as dense blue-grey camouflage, not calm thin snow over needle-covered shade. Serrated light islands with shaded rims are close to tree-footprint size and compete with the conifers in the forest composite; at 4x/8x the rims make them look like raised clumps. The same distinctive dark forks and snow islands recur every 288 px in the 3x3 field, producing obvious repeated rows/columns. Compared with the approved winter grass/plains and snowy paddies, nearly all snow is a uniform muted blue slab, without their small neutral-white snow accents. Rework into fewer, broader, flatter low-contrast snow drifts with quieter edges and irregular dark litter openings; use restrained matching snow highlights while retaining forest shade, then recheck the full repeat and tree composite.

fail.name: forest@winter-floor-base
fail.problems: Fails the calm-floor requirement: interlocking lobed snow shapes and hard dark-green gaps create an all-over camouflage pattern at 1x. Their bright upper rims and dark lower rims give many patches a bush/crown-like raised silhouette at 4x/8x, adding visual clutter directly between and behind tree trunks. The prominent forked snow bands recur every 288 px and form a readily traceable wallpaper repeat in the 3x3 composite. The predominantly blue-grey snow also sits apart from the neutral-white highlights of approved winter ground and paddies. Flatten the patch shading, simplify the serrated contours, group snow into larger unequal drifts separated by broad quiet shade/litter areas, and add only sparse compatible snow highlights; ensure the new arrangement conceals the repeat beneath trees.
